D.comparison: not using LLMs for everyday learning

cells.quote: 88% of participants adopted LLMs for learning.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive adoption proportion rather than a measured learning outcome; the comparison is the remaining 12% who did not adopt LLMs for learning.

D.treatment: EBP training with simulation and mentoring

result.effect: Mean 31.7 (SD 12.8) before training vs 120.9 (SD 7.4) after training; Wilcoxon Z=-6.3, p<0.001

cells.quote: All 4 items showed statistically significant improvement immediately after the training (all, p < 0.001).
cells.note: The skill outcome integrates multiple VAP-prevention procedures; the study does not state learners' prior knowledge of the taught content.

D.treatment: EBP training with simulation and mentoring followed by clinical implementation

result.effect: Mean 31.7 (SD 12.8) before training vs 121.4 (SD 9.4) during implementation; Wilcoxon Z=-6.3, p<0.001; 84.6% high performance during implementation

cells.quote: As illustrated in Figure 3, in which the skill scores were re-categorized into three levels: high, moderate and low scores, prior to the training, 100% of participants scored in the low category. Following the training, 88.5% achieved high score, and at the assessment during the implementation period, 84.6% maintained high performance level.
cells.note: The implementation assessment occurred after training, but the exact follow-up interval is not stated.

D.treatment: EBP training with simulation and mentoring

result.effect: Mean 6.0 (SD 1.7) before training vs 10.6 (SD 1.5) during implementation; Wilcoxon Z=-6.2, p<0.001

cells.quote: Knowledge and practice scores continued to improve significantly throughout the study period (all, p < 0.001).
cells.note: The study reports knowledge scores but does not specify the knowledge type beyond VAP-prevention knowledge.
